original.reason: The supplied original proof is truncated before any substantive argument or conclusion, so it cannot be verified as a complete proof.

judgment.reason: The stated finite-value lemma is not directly established: varying g(a) need not keep the b-side fixed when f(b)=a (and analogous collisions occur). Those cases require additional argument.
Its key observation has an unaddressed collision case: if f(b)=a, changing g(a) also changes g(f(b)), so the claimed direct conclusion does not follow as written.
The finite-support comparison omits coincident-index cases, notably f(v)=u, where varying g(u) changes both sides. Thus (*) is asserted without a complete proof.

The finite-value consequence is not proved in collision cases. Moreover, after proving fixedness only for x with f(x)≠f(a), it simply ignores the possible case f(x)=f(a), so the conclusion that every x is fixed does not follow.
